title: Fused Sampling and Grouping with Search Space Reduction for Efficient Point Cloud Acceleration
problem: Sampling and grouping layers in point-based DNNs incur high time and energy costs due to iterative point cloud data access and computation required for local feature extraction.
motivation: Efficient point cloud processing with deep neural networks is critical for real-time 3D perception applications.
method: The system organizes 3D points using Morton codes, which arrange points sequentially in memory while keeping spatially nearby points close together for fast access. Instead of performing sampling (selecting key reference points) and grouping (finding neighbors around each point) as separate operations, it fuses them into a single step that reuses distance calculations from previous iterations. Dedicated hardware is designed to efficiently execute these fused operations.
key_novelty: It fuses sampling and grouping in point cloud processing and organizes data with Morton codes to enable reuse of distance computations, reducing redundant calculations.
contributions: Morton code-based data structure enabling sequential access to points within voxels
Fused sampling and grouping approach with search space reduction through distance reuse
Dedicated hardware architecture optimized for point cloud processing
Efficiency gains without requiring model retraining

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: Reduced energy consumption via reduced distance calculations and data accesses

primary_theme: Hardware-accelerated point cloud DNN via memory-efficient data structures and fused operations
